_: Aluminium alloy 6061-T6 (Al-Mg-Si, solution treated and aged) at room temperature, bare machined / brushed, with its natural few-nm oxide: frames, rails, tools, furniture, fittings, bike parts. Anodised, polished and weathered as states. Partners research lane 11-07 (PARTNERS.md).

alpha.src: Ra by finish as for steel; brushed is anisotropic along the lines; no measured BRDF fit found

n.src: RAKIC98 Brendel-Bormann data file re-read 11-08 (refractiveindex.info database main/Al/nk/Rakic-BB.yml, CC0): 0.54147 um n 0.935 k 6.310, 0.56452 um n 1.016 k 6.552, interpolated at 550 nm n 0.965, k 6.40 (the Lorentz-Drude fit Rakic-LD gives 0.967 / 6.46); corrected from n 0.96, k 6.69 (k 6.69 sits near 570 nm)

F0.src: ((n-1)^2 + k^2)/((n+1)^2 + k^2) at 550 nm with n 0.965, k 6.40 (recomputed 11-08 after the n,k correction; was 0.921): the brightest common metal, near-neutral (slight dip ~800 nm)

F0_rgb.src: aluminium reflectance near-neutral (PBR practice tables, consistent with the n,k above)

n_k_550nm.src: RAKIC98 Brendel-Bormann data file re-read 11-08 (refractiveindex.info database main/Al/nk/Rakic-BB.yml, CC0): 0.54147 um n 0.935 k 6.310, 0.56452 um n 1.016 k 6.552, interpolated at 550 nm n 0.965, k 6.40 (the Lorentz-Drude fit Rakic-LD gives 0.967 / 6.46); corrected from n 0.96, k 6.69 (k 6.69 sits near 570 nm)

absorption.v: opaque metal; skin depth ~7 nm at 550 nm; the natural oxide (Al2O3, 2-5 nm, n 1.65) is optically invisible; anodic oxide (5-25 um) is a transparent porous dielectric over the metal and takes dye

static.src: ETB friction table re-read 11-08: aluminum on aluminum clean and dry 1.05-1.35, lubricated and greasy 0.3: soft, adhesive, galls and smears

kinetic.src: E: the sources disagree and the primary is not re-read: ETB re-read 11-08 lists 0.4 in its kinetic column for aluminum on aluminum clean and dry; Wikipedia's friction table (re-read 11-08) gives 1.4-1.5 marked 'citation needed'; MARKS 1.4 recalled from Marks' Handbook, not re-read; 1.4 kept; lubricated 0.1-0.3 E

friction.counterface: aluminium on aluminium (pairs/partners.json: steel, rubber.sole; pairs/skin.json: skin.glabrous)

surface_energy_mJ_m2.src: as metal.steel (MANTEL94-type behaviour: the hydrocarbon overlayer sets it)

restitution.src: ARYAEI10 aluminium lower than steel; not read as a number

E_star_GPa.src: E / (1 - nu^2) from E 68.9 GPa, nu 0.33 (half-space modulus; the soft partner's own E* combines in series)

contact_stiffness_kPa_per_mm.src: flat punch k = 2 E* a over area pi a^2, a 50 mm (hand-sized patch): an unyielding barrier next to any soft partner

hertz_constant_N_per_m1_5_R25mm.src: F = (4/3) E* sqrt(R) d^1.5, rigid sphere R 25 mm

contact_damping_ratio.src: zeta = -ln e / sqrt(pi^2 + ln^2 e) from restitution 0.75

restitution.src: ARYAEI10: aluminium balls / sheets give lower e than steel (softer, earlier plasticity); 0.7-0.8 taken at ~1 m/s, not read as a number

response_time_ms.src: Hertz contact time t = 2.87 (m^2/(R E*^2 v))^0.2, rigid 1 kg sphere, R 25 mm, 1 m/s: sub-millisecond; in a slap or a step the soft partner sets the pulse

damping_ratio.src: as contact_damping_ratio (energy lost per impact, from restitution)

solver._: Rigid next to body tissue. Thin aluminium (cans, foil, sheet) buckles and dents easily: yield 276 MPa but a third of steel's stiffness, so thin parts are a shell-buckling problem, not a contact-stiffness one.

water_contact_angle_deg.src: FIRGELLI degreased aluminium 67.3 deg (vendor calculator page, no primary source); behaviour as steel

porosity.src: wrought metal non-porous; the anodic oxide is a honeycomb of 10-30 nm pores (sealed after dyeing)

v.position: conductor, the zero of the scale (as metal.steel); anodised aluminium is an insulator on top and charges like a ceramic

triboelectric.src: ALPHALAB: all conductors about the same affinity

resistivity_ohm_m.src: ASM_6061 datasheet re-read 11-08 (ASM / MatWeb sheet MA6061T6, PDF at aerospacemetals.com; AA typical values, not for design): 3.99e-006 ohm-cm (3.99 uohm cm) at 68 F

hardness.src: ASM_6061 HB 95 (500 kg, 10 mm), HV 107 converted; Mohs E (pure Al 2.75)

abrasion.v: soft: scratches from steel, sand and even hard grit in cloth; bare aluminium greys a fingertip (oxide smears); anodised surfaces resist wear (Al2O3, ~HV 300-500)

poisson.src: ASM_6061 datasheet re-read 11-08 (ASM / MatWeb sheet MA6061T6, PDF at aerospacemetals.com; AA typical values, not for design): 0.33

shear_GPa.src: ASM_6061 datasheet re-read 11-08 (ASM / MatWeb sheet MA6061T6, PDF at aerospacemetals.com; AA typical values, not for design): shear modulus 26 GPa; E/(2(1+nu)) gives 25.9

yield_MPa.src: ASM_6061 datasheet re-read 11-08 (ASM / MatWeb sheet MA6061T6, PDF at aerospacemetals.com; AA typical values, not for design): T6 tensile yield 276 MPa

ultimate_MPa.src: ASM_6061 datasheet re-read 11-08 (ASM / MatWeb sheet MA6061T6, PDF at aerospacemetals.com; AA typical values, not for design): T6 UTS 310 MPa

elongation_pct.src: ASM_6061 datasheet re-read 11-08 (ASM / MatWeb sheet MA6061T6, PDF at aerospacemetals.com; AA typical values, not for design): elongation at break 12 % and 17 % (two specimen forms, 1/16 in sheet and 1/2 in round)

toughness_KIC_MPa_m05.src: ASM_6061 datasheet re-read 11-08 (ASM / MatWeb sheet MA6061T6, PDF at aerospacemetals.com; AA typical values, not for design): K_IC 29 MPa m^0.5 (TL orientation)

fatigue.v: no endurance limit: aluminium parts flexed repeatedly crack eventually (96.5 MPa at 5e8 cycles, ASM)
fatigue.src: ASM_6061 datasheet re-read 11-08 (ASM / MatWeb sheet MA6061T6, PDF at aerospacemetals.com; AA typical values, not for design): fatigue strength 96.5 MPa at 5e8 cycles, completely reversed (RR Moore)

thermal_expansion_1_K.src: ASM_6061 datasheet re-read 11-08 (ASM / MatWeb sheet MA6061T6, PDF at aerospacemetals.com; AA typical values, not for design): CTE 23.6 um/m-C (68-212 F)

sim._: Rigid for body contacts; shells buckle for thin parts.

conductivity_W_mK.src: ASM_6061 167 W/mK at 25 C (Wikipedia range 151-202 by temper)

heat_capacity_J_kgK.src: ASM_6061 datasheet re-read 11-08 (ASM / MatWeb sheet MA6061T6, PDF at aerospacemetals.com; AA typical values, not for design): 0.896 J/g-C

effusivity.src: sqrt(k rho c) = sqrt(167 x 2700 x 896) W s^0.5 m^-2 K^-1

contact_temp_with_skin_C.src: SKINTH: T = (e_skin 33 + e 20)/(e_skin + e), skin 33 C on material 20 C, e_skin 1188; lower = feels colder

emissivity.src: EMIS_ETB re-read 11-08: aluminum highly polished 0.039-0.057, foil 0.04, rough 0.07, commercial sheet 0.09, heavily oxidized 0.2-0.31, anodized 0.77; polished [0.03, 0.06] kept (0.03 E); brushed 0.05-0.1 E (between rough and commercial sheet); anodised upper 0.9 E

thermal_expansion_1_K.src: ASM_6061 datasheet re-read 11-08 (ASM / MatWeb sheet MA6061T6, PDF at aerospacemetals.com; AA typical values, not for design): 23.6 um/m-C

anodised.src: anodic Al2O3 5-25 um: a dielectric coat over the metal: matte-satin, dyeable (colour sits IN the clear porous layer: a coloured coat over a metal base), insulating, hard, high IR emissivity (EMIS_ETB 0.77); EMIS_ETB re-read 11-08: aluminum anodized 0.77

polished.src: mirror polish; dulls in weeks as oxide and handling haze it

weathered_oxidised.src: outdoor aluminium greys to a chalky dull oxide (white corrosion product, pitting near salt); not a rust: it protects itself

wet.src: water film between aluminium faces partly separates the adhesive junctions

oily.src: ETB friction table re-read 11-08: aluminum on aluminum lubricated and greasy 0.3 (MARKS 0.3, recalled, agrees)

cold.src: feels the coldest of the library's solids: effusivity ~20 100, contact temperature with skin ~20.7 C at 20 C ambient (wood.oak 29.3 C)

ETB.cite: The Engineering ToolBox, Friction and friction coefficients for some common materials
ETB.lic: free web reference; numbers used as facts (friction table re-read 11-08)

MARKS.cite: Marks' Standard Handbook for Mechanical Engineers, friction coefficient table (static/kinetic, dry and greasy, metals on metals)
MARKS.lic: paywalled handbook; numbers used as facts (recalled from the source, not re-read 11-07)

ALPHALAB.cite: Lee B / AlphaLab Inc. (TriField) triboelectric table, charge affinity nC/J (positive = charges +); zero = the average conductor (all metals about equal); read via the storiesinfabric.blogspot.com reprint 11-07
ALPHALAB.lic: free web table, reproduction only in whole: single numbers used as facts, table not copied STUDY ONLY (P13)

SKINTH.cite: skin thermal inputs for contact temperature: k 0.37 W/mK, c 3500 J/kgK (Duck 1990 tissue tables, typical), rho 1090 from skin.body

ASM_6061.cite: ASM Aerospace Specification Metals / MatWeb, Aluminum 6061-T6 datasheet (Aluminum Association typical values, 'not for design'): density 2.70, E 68.9 GPa, nu 0.33, G 26 GPa, yield 276, UTS 310 MPa, HB 95, K_IC 29, k 167 W/mK, c 0.896 J/gK, CTE 23.6e-6/K, resistivity 3.99 uohm cm, fatigue 96.5 MPa; density, E, HB and k read 11-07 via a PDF printout
ASM_6061.lic: MatWeb terms forbid redistributing the compilation: single numbers used as facts, STUDY ONLY (P13); re-read 11-08: every number in the cite matches the sheet

RAKIC98.cite: Rakic AD, Djurisic AB, Elazar JM, Majewski ML. Optical properties of metallic films for vertical-cavity optoelectronic devices. Appl Opt 37:5271-5283 (1998), Brendel-Bormann fit, via refractiveindex.info; data file re-read 11-08 (refractiveindex.info-database main/Al/nk/Rakic-BB.yml)
RAKIC98.lic: refractiveindex.info CC0; numbers used as facts

ARYAEI10.cite: Aryaei A, Hashemnia K, Jafarpur K. Experimental and numerical study of ball size effect on restitution coefficient in low velocity impacts. Int J Impact Eng 37:1037-1044 (2010)
ARYAEI10.lic: paywalled; finding (e falls with ball size, rises with sheet hardness) used

MANTEL94.cite: Mantel M, Wightman JP. Influence of the surface chemistry on the wettability of stainless steel. Surf Interface Anal 21:595-605 (1994)

EMIS_ETB.cite: The Engineering ToolBox, Emissivity coefficients of common products (re-read 11-08: stainless polished 0.075, weathered 0.85, type 301 0.54-0.63; aluminum highly polished 0.039-0.057, commercial sheet 0.09, rough 0.07, anodized 0.77; rubber hard glossy plate 0.94, natural hard 0.91, natural soft 0.86; plastics 0.90-0.97; no nylon row)
EMIS_ETB.lic: free web reference; numbers used as facts (re-read 11-08)

FIRGELLI.cite: Firgelli Automations, surface energy / contact angle calculator page: degreased aluminium water angle 67.3 deg (no primary source given)
FIRGELLI.lic: vendor web page; number used only as an estimate
